steps.message:
# Some coins misbehave in the flooded cave

### What happens
`recording.mp4` is an uncut run through a flooded cave basin. Partway through the clip, Tux does something that releases a group of new coins. From that moment until the end of the clip, those coins do not behave the way coins in this game should. The coins that were already placed in the level, Tux, the fish and the scenery in the recording are correct.

### Expected
The released coins should behave like a normal coin burst in this game, from the moment they spread out of the block until they come to rest and Tux swims back to collect them. Once a coin is in the water it should drift down slowly. Fix every way the released coins behave wrongly in the recording.

## Attached visual evidence

- `/app/.harbor_assets/recording.mp4` (44 seconds)

You can inspect individual moments of the video by extracting frames from it with `ffmpeg`.

Inspect the attached file before making changes.

steps.message:
I fixed the coin burst in three places and the game builds. I couldn't watch the recording: `/app/.harbor_assets/` is empty and there's no `recording.mp4` anywhere on the system. So I worked from the code that creates the burst from a block (`CoinExplode` spawning `HeavyCoin`s). I haven't played through a level with these fixes yet.

What I changed:

1. **The coins spread the wrong way** (`src/object/coin_explode.cpp`). The left/right sign was being applied to the vertical speed instead of the horizontal. So every coin flew to the same side, and half of them shot downward instead of arcing up. It's now `Vector(vector.x * side, vector.y)`, which gives the usual upward fan to both sides.

2. **The coins didn't come to rest** (`HeavyCoin::collision_solid`, `src/object/coin.cpp`). Any landing faster than 20 made the coin bounce again, so it kept hopping almost forever. Landing also never cleared its sideways speed, so it slid along the floor without stopping. Now only landings faster than 200 bounce, and a slower landing stops the coin completely.

3. **The coins ignored the water** (`HeavyCoin::update`). The released coins had no water handling at all and fell as fast as they would in air. They now check whether they are in water, the same way rocks already do. In water, gravity drops to 20%, falling speed is capped, and movement is slowed, so they drift down gently.

The coins already placed in the level, Tux and the fish use different code, so they aren't affected. If you can re-attach the recording, I'll check the fixes against what it shows.
